scope: Leader and nonleader native callee exec retire saved stopped-function contexts, follow the actual kernel TID replacement, retain failed event inspection for retry and release the replacement stop, including genuine signal resume, automatic forwarding and failed-detach retry. Live independent original-mm peers remain readable. x86-64, native i386, ARM64 4/64 KiB profiles. No universal compatibility claim.

reproduction.interpretation: Initial five-scenario thread driver failed 26 of 46 checks. Recompiled original production backend and original shared core with the current thread driver, removing only the new replacementTask API assertion absent from the original header. The original header is reconstructed byte-for-byte and its hash matches the previous snapshot. The expanded baseline fails 32 of 55 reached checks. Missing replacement readiness skips dependent liveness assertions. The current full driver requires 136 checks across leader/nonleader cases; all are mandatory.

previousSnapshots.note: Previous snapshots are historical evidence. No new single-CPU full concurrency claim.

resourceUse.nativeI386: Actual ELF32 target on the host kernel with copied i386 glibc/loader. Fixture linked to glibc CRT directly because host multilib libgcc is unavailable; no CPU emulation.

limitations: Required remote CI and release execution pending.

An already-exited leader, unrelated sibling exec, multiple borrowed contexts per group and orphan-detach callees require additional live coverage. Calls without TRACEEXEC and cleanup transfer to another old-mm process remain pending.
GP write rejection uses real EXEC wait status; does not prove every register bank was unchanged.
Private-page affinity proof requires stated proc-mem/mapping permissions.
Other architectures, managed runtimes, Wine/Proton/container variants and remote ownership/disconnect cases remain incomplete.
